claim.pdf_says: Format 6 (all-literal): "ALL literal-1" with ALL underlined. Format 7 (symbolic-character): "ALL symbolic-character-1" with ALL NOT underlined (verified at 300 dpi with the crop extended through the descender band).
claim.markdown_says:
Format 6 (all-literal):

ALL literal-1

Format 7 (symbolic-character):

ALL symbolic-character-1 - both transcribed as bare paragraph text, neither with a Figure-notes paragraph. The only record of Format 6's underline is an aside attached to the Format 5 figure: "> (i) For contrast, in Format 6 (`ALL literal-1`) the printed standard **does** underline `ALL`, making it required there." Format 7's underline state is recorded nowhere.
claim.why_it_matters: Underlining is what separates a required keyword from an optional word (8.3.1.1). Formats 1-5 on this page each carry a Figure-notes paragraph recording that `ALL` is NOT underlined there; Formats 6 and 7 carry none, so a markdown reader cannot tell that `ALL` is required in Format 6 and cannot see that the printed standard leaves `ALL` un-underlined in Format 7 even though `ALL symbolic-character-1` is not a figurative constant without it. That un-underlined `ALL` is an apparent ISO typesetting defect of exactly the kind the Figure notes exist to record, and it is currently invisible.

verdict.reasoning:
BOTH SOURCE OBSERVATIONS INDEPENDENTLY CONFIRMED, BUT THE CLAIM'S RATIONALE IS MATERIALLY WRONG ON TWO POINTS.

(1) PDF, verified by pixel measurement on E:/Temp/specrecon/v144/spec_p144.png (2550x3300 @ 300 dpi), not by eyeballing a downscaled render. Column/row ink profiles:
  - Format 6 glyph line y=2363-2393; words at x=[269,342] ('ALL') and x=[358,505] ('literal-1'). A 3-px rule sits at y=2408-2410 spanning x=[273,339] - i.e. squarely under 'ALL' and under nothing else. ALL IS UNDERLINED in Format 6. Confirmed.
  - Format 7 glyph line y=2600-2639 (2631-2639 is the descender of 'y' in 'symbolic', x=380-390); words at x=[269,342] ('ALL', identical metrics to Format 6) and x=[363,762] ('symbolic-character-1'). The entire band BELOW the descender, y=2643-2705 across x=240-1100, contains ZERO ink runs. Direct pixel check of the would-be underline box (y 2640-2670, x 265-360): min=255, mean=255.0 - pure white. The same box for Format 6 (y 2400-2420, x 265-360): min=32. ALL IS NOT UNDERLINED in Format 7. Confirmed, with the descender band fully included as the claim asserts.

(2) Markdown, verified verbatim at specs/ISO_COBOL.md lines 6218-6224: 'Format 6 (all-literal):' / blank / 'ALL literal-1' / blank / 'Format 7 (symbolic-character):' / blank / 'ALL symbolic-character-1'. Bare paragraph text - not even inside the ``` fences used for Formats 1-5 - and no Figure-notes block on either. Formats 1-5 each do carry one (lines 6178, 6187, 6196, 6205, 6214). The Format 6 underline is recorded only by the displaced aside at line 6216, hanging off the Format 5 notes. `grep -i underlin` cross-referenced against 'symbolic' returns nothing: Format 7's underline state is recorded nowhere in the document. Confirmed.

WHY THE CLAIM'S RATIONALE FAILS (and why the fix must not be written as described):
  - The claim says 'a markdown reader cannot tell that ALL is required in Format 6'. FALSE, and self-contradictory - the claim's own markdown_says field quotes line 6216 stating exactly that. The Format 6 fact is present, merely misfiled under Format 5.
  - The claim says 'ALL symbolic-character-1 is not a figurative constant without it [ALL]' and calls the un-underlined ALL 'an apparent ISO typesetting defect'. FALSE on both counts, per the spec itself: 8.3.2.2.29 (line 5639) - 'A symbolic-character is a user-defined figurative constant that represents a value specified in the SPECIAL-NAMES paragraph.' A bare symbolic-character-1 IS already a figurative constant, exactly as ZERO/SPACE/QUOTE are in Formats 1-5. 8.3.2.4.3 (line 5805) - un-underlined uppercase words 'are called optional words and may be specified at the user's option with no effect on the semantics of the format.' And GR 10 for Format 7 (line 6326) reads 'represents ONE OR MORE of the character...', the Formats 1-5 phrasing, whereas GR 3(b) (line 6274) singles out 'ALL literal-1' as the only form whose length comes from the literal. ISO's typesetting is therefore CORRECT and DELIBERATE: ALL is genuinely optional in Format 7 and genuinely required in Format 6. Recording it as an ISO defect would inject a spec-fidelity error.
  - The claim cites '8.3.1.1' for the underlining convention. No such section exists in the document. The governing sections are 8.3.2.4.2 (keywords: 'uppercase and underlined', line 5770) and 8.3.2.4.3 (optional words, line 5805).

WHAT SURVIVES, AND WHY IT IS STILL REAL AND STILL MEANING-BEARING: the markdown nowhere states that ALL is optional in Format 7. That is not cosmetic - it is the parser-visible fact that a bare `symbolic-character-1` (e.g. `MOVE BACKSPACE TO X` after `SYMBOLIC CHARACTERS BACKSPACE IS 9`) is a legal figurative constant reference, semantically identical to `ALL BACKSPACE`. Every other format on this page has that required/optional status stated explicitly; Format 7 alone has it stated nowhere, and the one adjacent aside ('For contrast, in Format 6 ... does underline ALL') contrasts Format 6 against Formats 1-5 and never mentions Format 7 at all. A reader can only infer Format 7's status from the absence of a note - inference, not transcription. This is a genuine omission of load-bearing content relative to the printed page, independently confirmed at the pixel level.
verdict.corrected_description: Confirmed, but re-scope and re-motivate it. GENUINE DEFECT: Formats 6 and 7 of 8.3.3.6.2 (specs/ISO_COBOL.md lines 6218-6224) are the only formats on page 144 transcribed as bare paragraph text with no Figure-notes paragraph, and the required/optional status of `ALL` in FORMAT 7 is recorded nowhere in the document. NOT A DEFECT, and to be dropped from the finding: (a) Format 6's underline IS already recorded, at line 6216, merely misfiled as an aside on the Format 5 notes block - it should be moved to a proper Format 6 Figure-notes paragraph, not treated as missing; (b) the un-underlined `ALL` in Format 7 is NOT an ISO typesetting defect. It is correct and deliberate: 8.3.2.2.29 defines a symbolic-character as itself a user-defined figurative constant, 8.3.2.4.3 makes un-underlined uppercase words optional 'with no effect on the semantics of the format', and GR 10 (8.3.3.6.4) uses the Formats 1-5 'one or more of the character' phrasing while GR 3(b) singles out `ALL literal-1` as the sole length-from-literal form. So `ALL` is optional in Format 7 exactly as in Formats 1-5, and `symbolic-character-1` alone is a legal figurative constant. Correct remediation: give Formats 6 and 7 their own Figure-notes paragraphs matching the page's convention - Format 6: '`ALL` IS underlined in the printed standard (required word); `literal-1` is not. Without `ALL`, literal-1 is an ordinary literal, not a figurative constant.'; Format 7: '`ALL` is NOT underlined - it is an optional word (8.3.2.4.3), so `symbolic-character-1` alone is already a figurative constant (8.3.2.2.29) and `ALL symbolic-character-1` is semantically identical.' Then relocate the line-6216 aside out of the Format 5 block. Also fix the claim's dead citation: the underlining convention is 8.3.2.4.2 / 8.3.2.4.3, not '8.3.1.1', which does not exist in this document. Severity is better read as 'annotation-omission' than 'incorrect-figure' - the transcribed glyph text of both formats is exactly right; only the underline metadata note is absent.
